doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: The Phillips uncles: Sid and Will Phillips
summary: Four bandleader uncles; Sid Phillips arranged for Ambrose, went to New York and jammed with swing players; Will conducted the Palladium band for Ellington and Goodman.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well I want to go back with you because I read that you came from a musical family and your uncles were in the business. Were you fascinated early on by — how much did you witness of what they did and was it something that seemed like oh yes, I want to do that.

Yeah it was very interesting. I mean my older — I mean there were four brothers and they were all band leaders and they all played different instruments. And two of them became — I would say sort of household names in England certainly but also, surprisingly, in America. My uncle Sid Phillips was our leading arranger and jazz clarinet player. He wound up playing with Louis Armstrong’s U.K. All-Stars. But he’d gone to New York for Irving Mills. He was the Ambrose band arranger which was a very popular dance band both here and in the States. And Irving Mills, who had his publishing, invited him to New York where he recorded with an amazing — I’ve got the recordings — an amazing New York session band which is basically a Saturday night swing club band. But he also was jamming with Bunny Berigan and Bobby Hackett and Bud Freeman. And he actually introduced Artie Shaw to Buddy Rich, whom he heard playing in a club with I think it might have been Bobby Hackett or Adrian Rollini or someone like that. And he said to Artie Shaw, “Oh you want to hire this guy, he’s really great.” And he also convinced Chappel’s, the publishers, to take on Jerry Gray, who they’d never heard of, before all the Glenn Miller stuff, so a very interesting guy. And after the war he led Britain’s leading Dixieland band and then my youngest uncle, Will Phillips, conducted at London Palladium so he actually conducted the band for Duke Ellington and Benny Goodman. So the union regulations, they weren’t allowed to bring their own bands. So Duke Ellington played with my uncle’s band with him leading it. So Ellington would thereafter introduce him as my band leader.
